protected_stage1_reuse.reuse_policy: consume the protected normalized gcd and Bézout trust spine; do not introduce a competing gcd definition or duplicate the Stage 1 Euclidean trace contract

problem_card.title: Certified linear Diophantine solvability extension
problem_card.normalized_statement: For integers a, b, and c, with (a,b) != (0,0), there exist integers x and y satisfying a*x + b*y = c if and only if gcd(|a|,|b|) divides |c|.

input_contract.gcd_normalization: d = gcd(|a|,|b|) is a positive natural number
input_contract.zero_target_policy: c = 0 is solvable by x = 0 and y = 0, and every positive d divides 0

object_certificate_separation.sought_object: whether the linear equation has an integer solution
object_certificate_separation.constructive_witness: integers x and y satisfying a*x + b*y = c
object_certificate_separation.unsatisfiable_obstruction: a nonzero remainder r in |c| = q*d + r with 0 < r < d

source_map.support_scope: classical two-variable linear Diophantine solvability theorem
normalized gcd, Bézout witness, accepted-certificate soundness, and exact authority chain
historical context only; does not support verbatim attribution of the modern integer solvability equivalence to Euclid

negative_exemplar.obstruction_meaning: the nonzero remainder proves that 21 does not divide 20; a solution would force every common divisor of 252 and 105 to divide 20

failure_risks.summary: Absolute-value or sign normalization may drift.
failure_risks.required_rejection: bind d to gcd(|a|,|b|) and divisibility to |c|

failure_risks.summary: The excluded (0,0) coefficient case may be silently widened.
The c = 0 case may be incorrectly rejected or treated as exceptional search failure.
failure_risks.required_rejection: retain the explicit zero-target solution and divisibility rule

failure_risks.summary: A protected Bézout witness may be scaled by the wrong factor.
failure_risks.required_rejection: verify c = k*d and x = k*x0, y = k*y0 for the constructive route

failure_risks.summary: Inputs or target may be substituted after witness production.
failure_risks.required_rejection: bind a, b, c and all Stage 1 identities exactly

failure_risks.summary: A false nonzero remainder may be presented as an obstruction.
failure_risks.required_rejection: verify |c| = q*d + r and 0 < r < d

failure_risks.summary: A competing gcd definition or duplicate Euclidean trace contract may fork the trust spine.
failure_risks.required_rejection: require protected Stage 1 reuse and prohibit replacement definitions

failure_risks.summary: Timeout, failed search, or producer error may be mislabeled unsatisfiable.
failure_risks.required_rejection: accept unsatisfiability only from a checked divisibility obstruction
retain candidate_only authority until an independent MATHCERT disposition

failure_risks.summary: The modern integer equivalence may be over-attributed to Euclid or inflated into arbitrary Diophantine completeness.

suggested_wp01.objective: emit deterministic constructive witnesses or exact divisibility obstructions while consuming the protected Stage 1 gcd contract

certification_route_sketch.independence_requirement: checker must not import or execute the MATHSOLVE producer

chaidez_documentary_contract.opening: begin with the positive 252x + 105y = 84 construction and the negative 252x + 105y = 20 obstruction

claim_boundary.statement: This Forge package fixes the modern theorem, protected Stage 1 reuse, two candidate exemplars, failure modes, and downstream contracts. It does not certify solvability or unsolvability, arbitrary Diophantine completeness, historical equivalence, novelty, or priority.
